body:
Full-codebase review, shared-test-case gaps. Verified.

Three rules are shared between the clients, each with a comment saying it must match the other client, and none has a shared case table: category canonicalisation, price-input parsing, and money/date formatting. Two of the three have already diverged (see the casing and price tickets) — good evidence that the table, not the comment, is what keeps a rule honest.

Also: Android's ExpenseMathTest asserts that every group in the table is non-empty; the web has no equivalent, so a renamed or emptied group would silently make the web's `it.each([])` iterate nothing while Android fails loudly. Add the same guard on the web side.

Fix direction: add `category-canon` and `price-parse` groups (and consider a formatting group), drive them from both suites, and mirror the group-coverage guard.
title: shared-test-cases: category canon, price parsing and formatting have no shared table
